title: Falafel
subtitle: Middle Eastern fried chickpea fritters
excerpt: The real thing: falafel made from dried soaked chickpeas (never tinned), blended with fresh herbs, onion, and spices, and fried until deeply golden and crisp outside while staying herb-green and slightly soft within.

recipe.sourceNotes: Falafel is a fried fritter made from ground legumes, most commonly chickpeas or fava beans, with fresh herbs and spices. The dish originated in Egypt (where fava beans are the traditional base) and spread throughout the Middle East, particularly to Lebanon, Israel, Jordan, and Palestine, where the chickpea version became the standard. Falafel is now eaten globally and is one of the most recognisable street foods in the world. The critical rule for making falafel is to use dried chickpeas soaked overnight rather than tinned; tinned chickpeas are cooked and too wet, producing a pasty falafel that falls apart in the oil. The dried chickpeas are blended raw after soaking, giving the falafel its characteristic rough texture and bright green interior from the herbs.

content.text: Dried chickpeas soaked overnight are non-negotiable; tinned chickpeas produce a pasty, falling-apart falafel. Do not over-process the mixture; it should be roughly textured, not smooth. If the mixture is too wet to hold its shape, add a tablespoon of flour. Test one falafel in the oil before frying the batch.

items.preparation: soaked overnight in cold water; drained; NOT cooked

content.text: Drain the soaked chickpeas thoroughly. Place them in a food processor with all the remaining ingredients except the oil. Pulse until the mixture is finely ground but still has texture; it should hold together when pressed but not be smooth.
Refrigerate the mixture for 30 minutes. Shape into balls or patties about the size of a walnut, pressing firmly.

Heat the oil to 175°C. Fry the falafel in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until deeply golden brown all over. Drain on kitchen paper. Serve in flatbread with hummus, tahini sauce, pickled cabbage, and sliced tomato.
